gaps.issue: The discriminator class F can be too weak or selected after results.
gaps.counterexample: Two output laws differ only on a test outside F and therefore have d_F=0.
gaps.corrected_now: F and K0 are typed as frozen parts of the claim.
gaps.unresolved_premise: A physically justified consumer geometry and precommitment.

gaps.issue: A numerical context metric may not track variation of the actual route.
gaps.counterexample: Two contexts are metrically close by interface labels but differ by an unrecorded route gate.
gaps.corrected_now: The metric is an explicit physical premise, not inferred from labels.

gaps.issue: The Lipschitz constant L can be unsupported or so large that the envelope is vacuous.
gaps.counterexample: A discontinuous hidden gate changes effect from zero to M at arbitrarily small declared distance.
gaps.corrected_now: Unknown/invalid L leaves UNRESOLVED; pointwise sharpness blocks a smaller assumption-free bound.
gaps.unresolved_premise: Physical/compositional derivation or independent calibration of L.

gaps.issue: The section r may be abstract rather than an actually realizable tested context.
gaps.counterexample: A representative state satisfies a fitted model but cannot be physically instantiated without changing the bearer/route.
gaps.corrected_now: Actual section realization is an all-of premise.

gaps.issue: Observed labels do not bound within-fiber physical diversity.
gaps.counterexample: The two-point hidden-fiber model has identical x and effects 0 versus M.
gaps.corrected_now: Exact non-entailment node and explicit delta penalty added.

gaps.issue: Sampling measure, independence or sensitivity can fail, and zero-measure contexts remain invisible.
gaps.counterexample: All large effects lie on a mu-null but physically admissible context.
gaps.corrected_now: Mass status is separated from amplitude/closure and all sampling premises are explicit.
gaps.unresolved_premise: A justified mu, dependence model and sensitivity floor.

gaps.issue: Distributional evidence and fitted kernels do not by themselves prove actual physical installation or familiar mineness.
gaps.counterexample: A shadow model reproduces every sampled law but is not read by the actual consumer.
gaps.corrected_now: R166 W1-W3/W6, R167 route actuality, C1 and B_min boundaries are retained.
gaps.unresolved_premise: Actual route/read audit, same-instance C1 admission and independent B_min.

failures.symptom: The audit rejected context-link descriptions containing 'not a replacement', 'analogous quantifier warning', and 'no envelope ... added' because it only recognized the literal words context or deduction.
failures.diagnosis: Checker vocabulary was narrower than the already explicit non-deductive semantics; the map links themselves were not deductive edges.
failures.repair: Require one of four exact non-deductive relation markers and rerun the complete audit.
failures.scope: Validation-code false failure only; no theorem, node, rule, source or exact result changed.

failures.symptom: build_map.py refused to run after the graph was already at R168 because its parent-hash guard requires the exact R167 input.
failures.diagnosis: The one-way builder was invoked twice; its guard correctly prevented applying the extension a second time.
failures.repair: Do not rebuild an already extended graph; verify the saved R168 graph with verify_round.py, which reconstructs and hashes the R167 prefix.
failures.scope: Expected idempotence safeguard; graph bytes and research claims were unchanged.
